title: Relative Mayer–Vietoris triangles and canonical derived exchange
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], with derived pullback computed by K-flat resolutions with flat terms and derived direct image by K-injective resolutions. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times_YY'$, with projections $g',f'$, and let $(U\subset X,p:V\to X)$ be an elementary distinguished square. Here $U$ is an open subspace of $X$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $p$ is representable etale, and $V\times_XE\to E$ is an isomorphism for the reduced closed subspace $E$ with underlying set $|X|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], the point sets carrying the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Put $T=U\times_XV$, and write $a:U\to Y$, $b:V\to Y$, $c:T\to Y$ for the composites. A prime denotes base change to $Y'$, so $T'=U'\times_{X'}V'$. For any $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $K'\in D(\mathcal O_{X'})$, the canonical relative Mayer–Vietoris triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$Rf_*K\longrightarrow Ra_*(K|_U)\oplus Rb_*(K|_V)\longrightarrow Rc_*(K|_T)\longrightarrow Rf_*K[1]$$
and the corresponding primed triangle for $K'$ are distinguished, naturally in the complexes. The first arrow has the two restriction components, and the second is the difference of restrictions to $T$; their boundary is the connecting arrow of the canonical resolution Mayer–Vietoris sequence. Applying $Lg^*$ to the first triangle, with the canonical finite-direct-sum and shift comparisons, again gives a distinguished triangle. Given any $\phi:L(g')^*K\to K'$, the canonical composites
$$\gamma_Z:Lg^*R(f_Z)_*(K|_Z)\longrightarrow R(f'_Z)_*L(g'_Z)^*(K|_Z)\longrightarrow R(f'_Z)_*(K'|_{Z'})\qquad (Z=X,U,V,T)$$
form a morphism from this $Lg^*$-image triangle to the primed triangle, with components $\gamma_X$, $\gamma_U\oplus\gamma_V$, $\gamma_T$, and $\gamma_X[1]$. Here $f_Z:Z\to Y$, $f'_Z:Z'\to Y'$, $g'_Z:Z'\to Z$, and the coefficient map is the pullback of $\phi$ transported by canonical pullback composition. Each exchange arrow is the adjunction mate whose transpose is
$$L(f'_Z)^*Lg^*R(f_Z)_*(K|_Z)\simeq L(g'_Z)^*L(f_Z)^*R(f_Z)_*(K|_Z)\longrightarrow L(g'_Z)^*(K|_Z),$$
using the counit of $L(f_Z)^*\dashv R(f_Z)_*$. In particular the square involving the connecting arrows commutes with these specified components, not just with an unspecified triangle completion. No isomorphism hypothesis on any $\gamma_Z$, and no quasi-compactness, properness, flatness, or boundedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For $Z=U,V,T$ put $E_Z=j_{Z!}j_Z^*$ and $H_Z=j_{Z*}j_Z^*$, using the exact slice restrictions. The sum-extension input gives the exact left adjunction $j_{Z!}\dashv j_Z^*$; the canonical module functors give $j_Z^*\dashv j_{Z*}$. Hence $E_Z\dashv H_Z$. Set $E_0=H_0=\mathrm{id}$, $E_1=E_U\oplus E_V$, $E_2=E_T$, $H_1=H_U\oplus H_V$, $H_2=H_T$. The elementary-square input supplies $0\to E_2\to E_1\to E_0\to0$ with signs $(+,-)$ then $(+,+)$, for both the original and every base-changed square. These are exact endofunctors; this is a sheaf-level resolution, not an assertion that a base-change map is invertible.

source.place: Tags 08GV, 08JK and 0DKH; expanded adjunction/cone compatibility using derived.tex Tags 0152 and 09T5

proof.text: Choose $K\to I$ K-injective with injective terms on the small etale site. Such resolutions exist in the stated universes. Apply the adjoint-sequence lemma to the exact sequence of step 1, with $P=f^*$, $F=f_*$, and its primed version with $P=f'^*$, $F=f'_*$, using their normalized derived adjunctions. The right mates give the degreewise split sequence $0\to f_*I\to f_*H_1I\to f_*H_2I\to0$. The canonical composition comparisons identify $R(f_*H_Z)K$ with $R(fj_Z)_*(j_Z^*K)$: $j_Z^*I$ is K-injective because $j_Z^*$ has the exact left adjoint $j_{Z!}$ of step 1 (a chain map $A\to j_Z^*I$ from an acyclic $A$ is the transpose of one from the acyclic $j_{Z!}A$ to $I$, hence null-homotopic, and homotopies transpose likewise); $Z$ need not be a scheme chart. So these are the usual derived restriction terms, and the comparisons preserve units and counits. Thus the two SES triangles are precisely the two displayed relative triangles: dualizing the sum evaluations gives the two restrictions, and dualizing $(+,-)$ gives their difference. The adjoint-sequence lemma gives naturality and resolution independence, with exactly the canonical SES boundary.

source.place: Tags 08GV, 08JK and 0DKH; expanded adjunction/cone compatibility using derived.tex Tags 0152 and 09T5

proof.text: The ringed-topos derived-pullback theorem says that $Lg^*$ is exact as a triangulated functor, with its canonical comparison on flat-term K-flat resolutions. It therefore takes the first triangle to a distinguished triangle. Its additivity identifies the middle term with the finite direct sum of the two pulled-back terms; insert its specified shift comparison at the last arrow. Neither this step nor step 2 uses quasi-coherence, quasi-compactness, boundedness, or a base-change isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 08GV, 08JK and 0DKH; expanded adjunction/cone compatibility using derived.tex Tags 0152 and 09T5

proof.text: Write $L_i=D(E_i)Lf^*$ and $L_i'=D(E_i')Lf'^*$. The chart-calculus composition isomorphism identifies $Lf'^*Lg^*$ with $L(g')^*Lf^*$. Etale sum base change then gives $\theta_i:L_i'Lg^*\simeq L(g')^*L_i$ for $i=0,1,2$. These compare whole left resolution diagrams: on a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ on $Y$, $f^*P$ and every $E_Zf^*P$ remain flat-term K-flat, by ringed pullback and sum-extension preservation. The left resolution is exact in each degree. Applying tensor pullback along $g'$ keeps it exact: by etale sum base change, with its counit and nested-slice compatibilities, $g'^*$ of the degree-$n$ sequence is identified with the base-changed elementary-square sequence for $(U'\subset X',V'\to X')$ evaluated at $g'^*f^*P^n$, which is exact by the base-change clause of the elementary-square node. (Equivalently, the quotient $f^*P^n$ is flat, so $g'^{-1}f^*P^n$ is flat over $g'^{-1}\mathcal O_X$ and the flat-quotient tensor lemma applies.) The summand comparison preserves evaluation for the second arrow and the two overlap counits with the signs $(+,-)$ for the first. Therefore it is a map of the short exact sequence diagrams on these representatives, not just three object isomorphisms. This verifies the resolution-diagram hypothesis of the adjoint-sequence comparison lemma.

source.place: Tags 08GV, 08JK and 0DKH; expanded adjunction/cone compatibility using derived.tex Tags 0152 and 09T5

proof.text: Apply that comparison lemma with $S=L(g')^*$, $T=Lg^*$, the three $\theta_i$ of step 4, and the given $\phi$. It yields a morphism of the particular triangles of step 2 and step 3, including their SES connecting arrows. Its $i$th component is transposed from $L_i'Lg^*R_iK\to L(g')^*L_iR_iK\to L(g')^*K\xrightarrow{\phi}K'$. To identify these components, transpose again across $j_{Z'!}\dashv j_{Z'}^*$. Preservation of the sum evaluation counits cancels $j_{Z'!}$ and its restriction, leaving $L(f'_Z)^*Lg^*R(f_Z)_*(K|_Z)\simeq L(g'_Z)^*L(f_Z)^*R(f_Z)_*(K|_Z)\to L(g'_Z)^*(K|_Z)\to K'|_{Z'}$. The composition comparisons preserve the relevant counits, so the first of these maps is exactly the specified exchange transpose and the last is the restriction of $\phi$. Adjunction bijectivity identifies the component with $\gamma_Z$. The finite-sum component is $\gamma_U\oplus\gamma_V$.

source.place: Tags 08GV, 08JK and 0DKH; expanded adjunction/cone compatibility using derived.tex Tags 0152 and 09T5

proof.text: The last square supplied in step 5 is consequently $\gamma_X[1]\,\delta_{Lg^*,K}=\delta_{K'}\,\gamma_T$, with the canonical shift comparison already inserted. The other two squares and the last component have likewise been identified with the specified restriction and difference maps and $\gamma_X[1]$. Thus every component is the one in the statement. The argument used arbitrary $K,K',\phi$ and arbitrary structural-ring pullback, so no additional isomorphism, flatness or boundedness hypothesis has entered.
